questions.question: Describe the roles of the chief in an early farming society.
questions.expected_answer: The chief led the chiefdom with his council, judged serious disputes, gave out land through his headmen, led the defence, and acted as a link to the royal ancestors, leading rain and first fruits ceremonies. He received tribute and was expected to be generous and care for the poor.

questions.question: Explain why cattle were so important, apart from food.
questions.expected_answer: Cattle were the main form of wealth. They were given as lobola or bohadi, which joined two families. They were slaughtered to honour the ancestors and at weddings and funerals. They were used to pay fines and given as gifts to make alliances.

questions.question: Explain how cattle helped a chief to keep his power.
questions.expected_answer: The chief had the largest herds, from tribute, fines and raids. Through mafisa or ukusisa he loaned cattle to poorer families, who used the milk and became loyal to him. He used cattle to feed people, reward followers and make alliances. A chief who did not share could lose followers.
